title: FDA Drug Safety Communication (2016): metformin and reduced kidney function
text: Metformin is contraindicated in patients with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2. Starting metformin in patients with an eGFR between 30 and 45 mL/min/1.73 m2 is not recommended. If eGFR later falls below 45 mL/min/1.73 m2 in a patient taking metformin, the benefits and risks of continuing treatment should be assessed. Metformin should be discontinued if eGFR later falls below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2.

title: Metformin prescribing information: lactic acidosis warning
text: Metformin-associated lactic acidosis is a rare but serious complication. The risk increases with renal impairment, hypoxic states and other acute conditions.

title: KDIGO 2022 Clinical Practice Guideline for Diabetes Management in CKD
text: In patients with type 2 diabetes and CKD, metformin can be used when eGFR is 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 or higher. The metformin dose should be reduced when eGFR falls below 45 mL/min/1.73 m2, and metformin should be stopped when eGFR falls below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2.

title: KDIGO 2022 Clinical Practice Guideline for Diabetes Management in CKD
text: SGLT2 inhibitors are recommended for patients with type 2 diabetes, CKD and an eGFR of 20 mL/min/1.73 m2 or higher. The glucose-lowering efficacy of SGLT2 inhibitors is reduced at lower eGFR.

title: KDIGO 2022 Clinical Practice Guideline for Diabetes Management in CKD
text: In patients with type 2 diabetes and CKD who have not achieved individualized glycemic targets despite metformin and SGLT2 inhibitor treatment, or who cannot use those medications, a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist is recommended.

title: DPP-4 inhibitor prescribing information: renal dosing
text: Most DPP-4 inhibitors such as sitagliptin require dose reduction when eGFR is reduced. Linagliptin does not require renal dose adjustment.

title: KDIGO 2022 Clinical Practice Guideline for Diabetes Management in CKD
text: Insulin requirements often fall as kidney function declines because renal insulin clearance decreases. Insulin doses may need reduction and the risk of hypoglycemia rises.

title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of CKD
text: CKD is classified by GFR category. G1 is 90 or above, G2 is 60 to 89, G3a is 45 to 59, G3b is 30 to 44, G4 is 15 to 29 and G5 is below 15 mL/min/1.73 m2.

title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of CKD
text: Hyperkalemia associated with renin-angiotensin system inhibitors can often be managed with measures that lower serum potassium rather than reducing the dose or stopping the inhibitor. The potassium and the RAS inhibitor regimen should be reviewed when potassium is elevated.

title: ACE inhibitor prescribing information: hyperkalemia
text: ACE inhibitors can cause hyperkalemia. Risk factors include renal insufficiency, diabetes, and concomitant potassium-sparing diuretics or potassium supplements. Serum potassium should be monitored.

title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of CKD
text: NSAIDs can reduce kidney function and precipitate acute kidney injury. Prolonged NSAID use should be avoided in advanced CKD and used with caution alongside RAS inhibitors and diuretics.

title: Warfarin prescribing information: drugs that increase bleeding risk
text: NSAIDs, including aspirin, increase the risk of bleeding when combined with anticoagulants such as warfarin. Patients on an anticoagulant should be monitored closely when another drug that affects bleeding is added.

title: Warfarin prescribing information: interacting drugs
text: Amiodarone can increase the anticoagulant effect of warfarin and raise the INR. Warfarin dose reduction and close INR monitoring are needed.

title: Warfarin prescribing information: pregnancy
text: Warfarin can cause fetal harm and is contraindicated in pregnancy except in women with mechanical heart valves at high risk of thromboembolism.

title: ACE inhibitor / ARB prescribing information: fetal toxicity boxed warning
text: ACE inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers carry a boxed warning for fetal toxicity. When pregnancy is detected they should be discontinued as soon as possible.

title: ACOG Practice Bulletin 222: Gestational hypertension and preeclampsia
text: Labetalol and long-acting nifedipine are first-line oral antihypertensive options in pregnancy. ACE inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers are avoided.

title: CredibleMeds: drugs with known risk of torsades de pointes
text: Drugs with a known risk of torsades de pointes, including amiodarone, sotalol, azithromycin, clarithromycin, citalopram, escitalopram, haloperidol, methadone, ondansetron, levofloxacin and moxifloxacin, prolong the QT interval. Combining two or more QT-prolonging drugs raises the risk of torsades de pointes and should be avoided or accompanied by ECG and electrolyte monitoring.

title: American Geriatrics Society 2023 Beers Criteria
text: For adults aged 65 and older the Beers Criteria list potentially inappropriate medications that should generally be avoided or used with caution. These include first-generation antihistamines such as diphenhydramine, benzodiazepines such as diazepam, lorazepam and alprazolam, non-benzodiazepine hypnotics such as zolpidem, sulfonylureas such as glyburide and glimepiride, tricyclic antidepressants such as amitriptyline, and skeletal muscle relaxants such as cyclobenzaprine. Chronic NSAID use should be avoided unless alternatives are not effective.

title: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes 2024: glycemic goals
text: An A1C goal below 7% is appropriate for many nonpregnant adults. Less stringent goals such as below 8% may be appropriate for older adults or people with limited life expectancy, advanced complications or extensive comorbid conditions.

title: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes 2024: pharmacologic approaches
text: Treatment regimens should be reviewed and modified every 3 to 6 months to achieve and maintain individualized glycemic goals. Delay in intensifying therapy when goals are not met, known as therapeutic inertia, should be avoided.

title: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes 2024: hypertension
text: For people with diabetes and hypertension a blood pressure target below 130/80 mmHg is recommended if it can be safely attained.

title: KDIGO 2021 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Blood Pressure in CKD
text: For adults with high blood pressure and CKD, treatment to a systolic blood pressure below 120 mmHg using standardized office measurement is suggested when tolerated.

title: Drug allergy: a 2022 practice parameter update
text: Penicillins should be avoided in patients with a documented penicillin allergy pending allergy evaluation. Cross-reactivity between penicillins and cephalosporins is low overall and depends mainly on shared side chains. Cephalosporins with dissimilar side chains can often be used when clinically necessary, with appropriate caution.

title: FDA Guidance for Industry: Drug-Induced Liver Injury, Premarketing Clinical Evaluation
text: An alanine aminotransferase (ALT) elevation above three times the upper limit of normal is a signal of potential hepatotoxicity. In a patient taking a potentially hepatotoxic drug it warrants clinical review, repeat testing and consideration of interrupting the drug.

title: NICE NG5: Medicines optimisation
text: A structured medication review should check that each medicine still has an indication. Medicines that are no longer needed, for example when the condition they treat has resolved, should be considered for discontinuation.

title: KDIGO 2012 Clinical Practice Guideline for Acute Kidney Injury
text: Acute kidney injury is defined as an increase in serum creatinine of at least 0.3 mg/dL within 48 hours, or an increase to at least 1.5 times baseline within the previous 7 days, or urine volume below 0.5 mL/kg/h for 6 hours.

title: Statin prescribing information: myopathy and rhabdomyolysis warning with fibrates
text: Combining a statin with a fibrate (especially gemfibrozil or fenofibrate) significantly increases the risk of severe myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.

title: NSAID prescribing information: bleeding risk with SSRIs
text: Concomitant administration of an NSAID with a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) produces an additive risk of upper gastrointestinal bleeding.

title: KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline: dual RAAS blockade warning
text: Combination of an ACE inhibitor with an ARB or direct renin inhibitor (dual RAAS blockade) is not recommended due to increased risks of hyperkalemia, acute kidney injury, and hypotension without clinical benefit.

title: Metformin prescribing information: iodinated contrast media precautions
text: Metformin should be withheld prior to or at the time of iodinated contrast imaging procedures in patients with eGFR between 30 and 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 to prevent contrast-induced acute kidney injury and lactic acidosis.

title: NICE Medicines Optimisation: Duplicate Therapy Warning
text: Prescribing multiple medications from the same therapeutic class without explicit clinical justification increases adverse event risk and medication burden.
